workstreams.summary: Imports, provider execution, database-backed code units, source navigation, and a multi-provider visualizer are established across several language and binary workflows. The 65,195-class QA APK completed all 10 DEX files in an isolated run in 6,924 seconds: 65,190 Java units were returned and all 65,190 were copied to derived storage (183,388,129 bytes). The DEX provider now retains discovered and returned method counts and truncation status; task settlement persists class, method, and failure observations; and the visualizer separately shows discovered, returned, and database-indexed method counts. Focused provider, task-executor, API, and component checks pass (59), with TypeScript and ESLint clean. The live QA project has two older completed runs that stored only 500 of 65,195 class identities and no method rows; a fresh run is still needed to verify current database ingestion and AI retrieval. The Java DEX class path now defaults to bounded batches of 8, with existing adaptive split retries for timeout, memory, and panic failures; focused Docker analyzer tests pass (14), and the LAN analyzer is healthy with batch size 8. A fresh analyzer-level QA probe completed all 10 DEX files in 4,835 seconds with batch size 8, returning 65,190 Java files; the prior one-class run took 6,924 seconds. Returned source bytes differed by 147,100, so file-level output parity remains unverified. A standalone structured pass counted 416,783 implemented DEX methods while returning 10,000; at that checkpoint, call and reference output each stopped at 4,000. The Rust prepass now counts all implemented methods before applying the response cap, and the rebuilt analyzer is healthy. The QA probe bypassed the webapp task persistence path; database ingestion and AI retrieval remain unverified. The coverage inventory now reconciles discoveredMethodCount, returnedMethodCount, and indexed function observations for newly executed DEX tasks. The Rust structured DEX pass now writes bounded 1,000-method pages; the analyzer streams them as NDJSON, and the DEX provider stages observations in run-scoped batches before atomic promotion on success. Docker QA against the stored 6.79 MB APK discovered and streamed all 33,401 methods across 34 pages, reported no method truncation, and removed temporary pages. A separate full structured pass against the larger APK returned all 416,783 methods across 417 pages. Task-executor tests cover pending-source promotion and type-check passes after regenerating Prisma from this checkout. This verifies analyzer transport and source-level persistence logic, not a real project task or AI retrieval. Rust DEX analysis now writes call and reference spill pages of 1,000 rows, bounded to 4,200 pages per evidence type and 256 MiB combined. The Python analyzer validates page names and counts before NDJSON delivery and removes temporary pages; the webapp validates and persists call edges plus field/string references in run-scoped batches. The analyzer image builds; 15 focused Docker analyzer tests, 5 provider tests, and a clean package-lock-based webapp type-check pass. The full QA APK task through the current provider, database, MCP, and AI context remains unverified.
